slot.brief: Classical probability with a small sample space (dice/cards); find probability of a compound event, possibly using independence.

stem: Two fair dice are rolled. Given that their sum is even, find the probability that their product is divisible by $3$.

verdicts.working: Given an even sum, both dice have the same parity: 18 equally likely outcomes. Of these, 8 have neither die divisible by 3, so the probability the product is divisible by 3 is (18−8)/18 = 5/9.

working:
Even-sum outcomes: $18$. Favorable outcomes: even-even pairs with a $6$ ($5$), or odd-odd pairs with a $3$ ($5$); $P=\dfrac{10}{18}=\dfrac{5}{9}$.

Independent check: Given an even sum, both dice have the same parity: 18 equally likely outcomes. Of these, 8 have neither die divisible by 3, so the probability the product is divisible by 3 is (18−8)/18 = 5/9.
solution:
An even sum means both dice have the same parity, giving $18$ equally likely outcomes. Among even-even outcomes, $5$ contain a $6$; among odd-odd outcomes, $5$ contain a $3$.
$$P(\text{product divisible by }3\mid\text{even sum})=\frac{5+5}{18}=\frac{5}{9}$$
